{
  "IP": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Shift operand and result data",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "The operand word is shifted or rotated according to the requested operation and returned as the result; the shifter's operation depends on this data.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The operand is held and transformed internally and the resulting word is exposed on res_o, so an integrator may need confidentiality for the data and an observer could read it at lines 111 and 143; internal assignments to sreg and bs_result can alter the shifted result at lines 95, 99, 101 and 138.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C",
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe res_o to disclose operand-derived data or corrupt the internal operand/result path so that the returned shift result is incorrect.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "rs1_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "res_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        95,
        122,
        123
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        95,
        99,
        101,
        122,
        128,
        129,
        138
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        111,
        143
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Shift amount",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "The shift distance determines how far the operand is shifted and therefore which result the operation returns.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The shift amount is copied into the serial step counter and selects barrel-shifter stages at lines 94, 128 and 129, so changing it can make the operation return an incorrect result.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could change shamt_i so the unit performs the wrong number of shifts and returns an incorrect result.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "shamt_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        94,
        128,
        129
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        94
      ],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Shift execution progress and sign-extension control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Information": "In the serial implementation, busy state, remaining steps and completion state determine whether and when the operation finishes; the sign-fill control determines how arithmetic right shifts treat the operand.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The unit internally assigns busy, count, completion and sign-fill control state at lines 80, 81, 82, 86, 88, 90, 94, 97 and 123, and corruption can cause an invalid completion or result; valid_o and res_o release behavior depends on this state at lines 110 and 111, so corrupting it can withhold or block completion.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could corrupt the progress state or sign-fill control so the shifter reports completion incorrectly, produces a wrong result, or remains busy without releasing valid_o.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "ctrl_i",
        "shamt_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "valid_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        94,
        123
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        80,
        81,
        82,
        86,
        88,
        90,
        94,
        97,
        123
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        110,
        144
      ]
    }
  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Shift instruction and function selection",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C3",
      "Why Not Kept": "The instruction function fields only select the supported operation or its result form, so Operation selectors treats them as part of the operation rather than as a separate conceptual asset."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Completion and busy status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C3",
      "Why Not Kept": "busy, done and valid_o describe or release the coprocessor's progress, which the Coprocessor progress state rule keeps as one operation-level concept."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Barrel-shifter intermediate values",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "C1",
      "Why Not Kept": "bs_level and the registered result path are working values or copies within the shifted data computation, not separate information."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Clock and reset",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "The clock and reset only time or initialize the unit's state at lines 79, 84, 135 and 137, so the Clocks and resets rule bars them as conceptual assets."
    },
    {
      "Candidate Name": "Fast-versus-serial implementation choice",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_cpu_cp_shifter",
      "Merged Into": "",
      "Why Not Kept": "FAST_SHIFT_EN is a build-time generic at line 23 that selects generated logic at lines 74-75 and 118-119 and cannot be changed or withheld at run time."
    }
  ],
  "Notes": []
}

conceptual assets.information: The operand word is shifted or rotated according to the requested operation and returned as the result; the shifter's operation depends on this data.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The operand is held and transformed internally and the resulting word is exposed on res_o, so an integrator may need confidentiality for the data and an observer could read it at lines 111 and 143; internal assignments to sreg and bs_result can alter the shifted result at lines 95, 99, 101 and 138.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe res_o to disclose operand-derived data or corrupt the internal operand/result path so that the returned shift result is incorrect.

conceptual assets.information: The shift distance determines how far the operand is shifted and therefore which result the operation returns.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The shift amount is copied into the serial step counter and selects barrel-shifter stages at lines 94, 128 and 129, so changing it can make the operation return an incorrect result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could change shamt_i so the unit performs the wrong number of shifts and returns an incorrect result.

conceptual assets.concept: Shift execution progress and sign-extension control
conceptual assets.information: In the serial implementation, busy state, remaining steps and completion state determine whether and when the operation finishes; the sign-fill control determines how arithmetic right shifts treat the operand.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The unit internally assigns busy, count, completion and sign-fill control state at lines 80, 81, 82, 86, 88, 90, 94, 97 and 123, and corruption can cause an invalid completion or result; valid_o and res_o release behavior depends on this state at lines 110 and 111, so corrupting it can withhold or block completion.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could corrupt the progress state or sign-fill control so the shifter reports completion incorrectly, produces a wrong result, or remains busy without releasing valid_o.

considered, not kept.reason: The clock and reset only time or initialize the unit's state at lines 79, 84, 135 and 137, so the Clocks and resets rule bars them as conceptual assets.
FAST_SHIFT_EN is a build-time generic at line 23 that selects generated logic at lines 74-75 and 118-119 and cannot be changed or withheld at run time.
